why: Found at the build, before any P5 outcome was compared: rule RC2 of the contract sets the annotated record's triage to 'annotated', but the frozen record schema schemas/result_record.schema.json (v1, which gate G9 validates every record against) admits triage only in finding, intent_question, model_defect and none, so a record carrying RC2's value can never be valid. The amended test reads RC2's mark where the build writes it, the record's annotation (annotation.triage 'annotated', with the annotation's source and text), and the record keeps the triage of a REFUTED record (finding). P5's claim is unchanged: both receives REFUTED and replayed, the Rollup's annotated with the whitepaper's source, the messenger's not. The contract docstring is pinned by sha256 and keeps RC2's wording; the report states the difference.

Correction of the line above: the inconsistency was found after the first local run of the contract tests, in which P5 had passed with RC2's triage 'annotated'; the bundle gate's G9 (v1 validity of every bundle record) then rejected that record. The amendment moves where the test reads the mark, not what P5 claims.

I34 (holon-rules/1.12, rule SYM, landing after I86) chains a new catalog version over 1.11, so M3 derives with 1.12 and every M3 law, I86's seventeen included, carries rule_catalog_version holon-rules/1.12 (scheme 2: no statement hash moves). C1 asserted catalog_version('M3') == thresholds.catalog (holon-rules/1.11) and took 1.11's base as the newest version other than 1.11, which becomes 1.12: it turns red at any later bump without saying anything about I86's rules. The amended test keeps I86's claim and drops the pin: M3's version is thresholds.catalog or later and keeps its six producer objects (assertIs); thresholds.catalog holds the six sub-forms; its base is the newest version below it (1.10), whose every producer it holds unchanged.

I34 (holon-rules/1.12, rule SYM, landing after I86) chains a new catalog version over 1.11, so M3 derives with 1.12 and every M3 law, I86's seventeen included, carries rule_catalog_version holon-rules/1.12 (scheme 2: no statement hash moves). C2 asserted each of the seventeen laws' rule_catalog_version == thresholds.catalog (holon-rules/1.11), which turns red at any later bump. The amended test keeps I86's claim and drops the pin: laws/M3 holds exactly the basis ids per sub-form and prefix, each with its rule and subform, and each carries M3's current catalog version (which C1 checks is thresholds.catalog or a later version keeping its producers).
